[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' was recorded in '''Desertoghill parish, barony of Coleraine, County Londonderry, Ireland''', in the '''1796 flax growers' list'''. The published transcription records an award of '''two spinning wheels'''.<ref name="Flax1796">W. Macafee, ''1796 Flaxgrowers' List for Co. Londonderry [T3419]'', sorted by surname, barony and parish, dated 21 February 2011, printed p. 49, record 2070: John Glasgow, Coleraine barony, Desertoghill [Desartoghill], two wheels. [https://www.billmacafee.com/1796flaxgrowerslist/1796flaxgrowersderry.pdf#page=49 Published transcription]. The compiler cites archival reference T3419; this citation is to the transcription rather than an independently inspected original list.</ref>

The entry gives his name and parish but no townland, age, wife or children. His birth and death dates have not yet been established.<ref name="Flax1796" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Possible move from Londonderry to Antrim ===

The 1851 census of Lisnagaver records '''[[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]]''', aged '''50''', as born in '''County Antrim''', while his brother '''[[Glasgow-2908|Samuel Glasgow]]''', aged '''60''', was born in '''County Londonderry'''. Their recorded ages suggest births about '''1801''' and '''1791''' respectively.<ref name="Lisnagaver1851">W. Scott and W. Macafee, ''1851 Census for some Parishes and Townlands in the Barony of Kilconway, Co. Antrim'', dated 7 May 2014, printed p. 141, Lisnagavor household 34, references 16848–16851. John Glasgow: head, 50, farmer, born Antrim; Samuel Glasgow: brother, 60, linen weaver, born Londonderry. [https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1851censuskilconway.pdf#page=141 Published census transcription].</ref>

'''If John of Lisnagaver was this man's son, and Samuel was also his son, the family likely moved from County Londonderry to County Antrim between about 1791 and 1801''': after Samuel's birth in Londonderry and before John's birth in Antrim. This John's appearance in the '''1796 Desertoghill flax list''' would provisionally narrow that move to '''between 1796 and about 1801'''.<ref name="Flax1796" /><ref name="Lisnagaver1851" />

This remains a migration hypothesis dependent on the proposed family identification. The dates are approximate, and a child's birthplace does not necessarily establish the parents' usual residence.

=== Identity ===

This profile documents the John Glasgow named in the 1796 Desertoghill entry. Whether he was the same man as another John Glasgow already represented on WikiTree remains unresolved.

=== Possible identification with John Glasgow of Inishrush ===

The Glasgow surname research catalogue identifies the flax-list entry as a possible earlier record of '''[[Glasgow-822|John Glasgow]]''', born in 1767, husband of Mary Arthur and associated with Inishrush before emigrating to Ohio. However, the catalogue explicitly leaves this identification unproved: the parish differs, and the flax list supplies no family details connecting the two records.<ref name="InishrushResearch">Glasgow Surname Project, [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/people/glasgow-822.html research dossier for John Glasgow, Glasgow-822], source assessment of the 1796 County Londonderry flax-premium list and discussion of the 1831 Inishrush household. Research synthesis, not an independent record of the proposed identification.</ref>

'''[[Glasgow-3927|John Glasco]]''' represents the head of household 2 at Inishrush in the 1831 census and is itself a proposed identity match for Glasgow-822. It does not independently identify the Desertoghill flax grower.<ref name="InishrushResearch" />

=== Possible identification with the father of John Glasgow of Lisnagaver ===

Another possibility is that this man was the '''John Glasgow, farmer''' named as the father of '''[[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow of Lisnagaver]]''' when the younger John married Margaret Garvin on '''16 November 1846''' at Second Garvagh Presbyterian Church.<ref name="Marriage1846">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, Coleraine registration district, Second Garvagh Presbyterian Church, Errigal parish, County Londonderry, entry 13: John Glasgow and Margaret Garvin, 16 November 1846. [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1846/09306/5369439.pdf Register image, IrishGenealogy.ie].</ref>

Margaret's residence was recorded as '''Rockfield, Desertoghill parish''', providing a geographical lead for further investigation. However, the marriage does not give the groom's father's residence or establish that he was the John recorded in the 1796 flax list.<ref name="Marriage1846" />

A possible identification concerns John Glasgow, Loughinsholin freeholder, 1831. The 16 August 1831 declaration lists Robert Glasgow and John Glasgow among freeholders of the barony printed Loughinshollen (modern Loughinsholin), County Londonderry, supporting Sir Robert Bateson. They are co-signatories; no kinship, occupation, age or individual townland is given. Castledawson and 4 July 1831 refer to the opposing meeting discussed in the declaration, not their homes or their signing date.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 16 August 1831, p.3, Loughinshollen freeholders’ declaration; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390548642/ record].</ref> [[Glasgow-2058]], [[Glasgow-3927]] (an indexed freeholder with uncertain locality), [[Glasgow-2990]] and [[Glasgow-4090]] remain adult regional comparisons. No same-name co-signature establishes descent, brotherhood or identity with the Cookstown merchant. The declaration concerns a holding in the barony, not necessarily residence there. The identification remains uncertain.

=== Possible John Glasco in Irish rosters, 1798–1799 ===
John Glasco is PRESENT at the Black-Rock Association meeting 8 May 1798.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1214061848/ The Public Register, or, Freeman's Journal, 1798-05-29, p.4].</ref>

John Glasco appears in the 24 September 1799 roster, continued beneath an earlier COUNTY OF LONDONDERRY heading.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1214179229/ The Public Register, or, Freeman's Journal, 1799-09-24, p.2].</ref>

The two entries retain separate identities: the 1798 Black-Rock attendee is not proved to be the 1799 County Londonderry roster bearer. A shared surname and county do not establish relatives.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4090]]. Possible 1799 Desertoghill contemporary, born before 1772; no roster link.

=== Possible John Glasgow, Allegheny Township list in Huntingdon County context, 1799 ===
John Glasgow is named under Allegheny Township in a township-grouped list accompanying Huntingdon County election-meeting material.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/587806805/ The North American (Philadelphia), 1799-09-10, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1140587856/ Pennsylvania Weekly Telegraph (Oracle of Dauphin and Harrisburgh Advertiser), 1799-09-18, p.2].</ref>

The two issues repeat one list. Allegheny Township was then in Huntingdon County and later in Cambria County, so the county labels are compatible. The list does not establish a father-and-son relationship with a 1790 household head.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4090]]. Broad uncertain before 1772 birth permits adulthood; Irish locality statement supplies no migration or individual connection to this record.

=== Possible John Glasgow, Carlisle postal addressee, 1793 ===
John Glasgow, care of William Brown, Esq., is an addressee in the Carlisle post-office list headed 1 January 1793.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1033763029/ The Carlisle Gazette, and the Western Repository of Knowledge, 1793-03-06, p.1].</ref>

"Care of William Brown, Esq." is the address qualification, not evidence of kinship. A postal entry alone does not establish that its addressee was alive on the list date.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4090]]. Broad uncertain before 1772 birth permits adulthood; Irish locality statement supplies no migration or individual connection to this record.

=== Possible John Glasgow, Millrig labourer and Kirkliston subscription, 1798 ===
John Glasgow, labourer, Millrig, is named among voluntary subscriptions in the parish of Kirkliston.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601860386/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1798-07-20, p.6].</ref>

This is a named labourer at Millrig in Kirkliston parish. It does not connect him to the Irish Johns, the Carlisle addressee or the Allegheny list.

This may concern [[Glasgow-4090]]. Broad uncertain before 1772 birth permits adulthood; Irish locality statement supplies no migration or individual connection to this record.
